summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of diastolic heart failure, COPD, atrial fibrillation, and diabetes was admitted for progressive dyspnea and hypertensive urgency, leading to flash pulmonary edema and respiratory failure requiring intubation. She was treated with IV diuresis, transitioned to oral torsemide, and managed for acute kidney injury due to overdiuresis, which resolved with supportive care. She developed a ventilator-associated pneumonia and a multidrug-resistant E. coli urinary tract infection, both treated with a 7-day course of meropenem. Her insulin was adjusted for glycemic control, and she received treatment for cutaneous candidiasis. She improved over 13 days, was weaned off the ventilator, and discharged to extended care on home medications, including diuretics, insulin, and antibiotics completed in hospital. Follow-up was advised for anticoagulation evaluation in atrial fibrillation and monitoring of abdominal hernias.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
MDR E. coli urinary tract infection
